question: The nineteenth-century French economist Frederic Bastiat spent most of his life tearing bad ideas apart in short, witty essays. But in 1850 in Paris, just before tuberculosis killed him, he published one book laying out his own positive theory of a free economy. What is its short title?
context: Harmonies economiques (Guillaumin, 1850) was Bastiat's positive treatise, cut short by his December 1850 death. Source: grokipedia.com/page/Frederic_Bastiat.
